A_general.open_code_note: No official public Ashby MCP repository or package was found in the prepared evidence. The official documentation identifies the hosted endpoint, but does not provide source code.
A_general.release_status: Open Beta; official knowledge-base title labels the server Beta.
other_official_servers: Ashby Assistant, Custom Agents, and Ashby Slack app are described as other first-party AI experiences; they are not identified as MCP endpoints.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Ashby says the MCP server is available on all Ashby plans, except Analytics-only organizations. No separate MCP price is stated.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Foundations at $400/month for companies with up to 100 employees. Plus and Enterprise prices are not listed there.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Ashby says pricing depends on company size, usage, and commitment; annual commitments may receive a 10% discount. MCP-specific billing or usage charges are not stated.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An Org Admin must enable the MCP Server toggle. Once enabled, Elevated Access users can connect their own accounts. Analytics-only organizations are excluded. Documented limits: 120 requests/minute per auth token and 120 tool-budget units/minute per user-and-organization pair; most calls cost 1 unit and filter_records costs 2.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization admin; user access also follows the user's existing Ashby permissions.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official documentation lists 17 tools: 12 read-oriented data and documentation tools, four recruiting write tools, and submit_mcp_feedback. The docs state that the available set grows over time and that tool inputs and outputs may change without notice. The Claude connector directory lists 16 tools and omits submit_mcp_feedback.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool schemas and response structures are not published in the reviewed official materials. Documentation gives functional summaries and notes that inputs and outputs may change.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth bearer authorization is advertised by the endpoint. See Authorization entry for the provided metadata.

MCP-specific logging and audit behavior is not described in the reviewed official documentation.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.ashbyhq.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="openid mcp offline_access". Protected-resource metadata identifies resource https://mcp.ashbyhq.com/mcp/v1, authorization server https://mcp-auth.ashbyhq.com/oidc, supported scopes ["openid","mcp","offline_access"], and bearer method ["header"]. Authorization-server metadata lists authorization endpoint /oidc/auth, token endpoint /oidc/token, registration endpoint /oidc/reg, PKCE S256, grant types ["implicit","authorization_code","refresh_token"], token endpoint auth methods ["client_secret_basic","client_secret_jwt","client_secret_post","private_key_jwt","none"], and token signing algorithms ["HS256","RS256","PS256","ES256","Ed25519","EdDSA"]. Token lifetime and revocation details were not supplied.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated POST evidence is HTTP 401 with JSON body {"error":"Unauthorized"}. OAuth metadata is JSON as summarized above.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth protected-resource metadata plus dynamic client registration. Provided raw metadata: endpoint response HTTP 401; WWW-Authenticate scope="openid mcp offline_access". Protected-resource documents return HTTP 200 and scopes_supported ["openid","mcp","offline_access"], bearer_methods_supported ["header"]. Authorization-server metadata returns registration_endpoint https://mcp-auth.ashbyhq.com/oidc/reg, code_challenge_methods_supported ["S256"], grant_types_supported ["implicit","authorization_code","refresh_token"], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["client_secret_basic","client_secret_jwt","client_secret_post","private_key_jwt","none"]. Token lifetime and revocation are NOT FOUND in supplied metadata.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tool list shows read tools and four recruiting write tools; the docs do not publish MCP tool annotations such as readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint. 2. add_note_to_candidate drafts a note for confirmation before saving; docs do not establish a server-enforced confirmation mechanism. Ashby says users can set approval controls in their MCP client. 3. OAuth is per user; docs say the server inherits existing Ashby permissions. Org Admin must enable the feature; only Elevated Access users can connect, and Analytics-only organizations are excluded. OAuth metadata exposes scopes openid, mcp, offline_access. Client allowlists, redirect URI approval policy, token lifetime, and revocation are Unknown. 4. No read-only mode, tool filters, query-free mode, sandbox, or region-specific endpoint is documented. 5. Ashby says returned data is limited to what the user can see; tool list includes candidate profiles with resumes, communications, notes, and transcripts. No MCP-specific field masking or PII exclusions are documented. 6. Limits: 120 requests/minute per auth token; 120 tool-budget units/minute per user-organization pair; most calls cost 1 unit, filter_records costs 2. No result truncation or bulk caps documented. 7. MCP parameter validation or correction behavior is Unknown; schemas are not published. 8. MCP audit logging and telemetry behavior are Unknown. 9. submit_mcp_feedback sends feedback to Ashby; description asks users to include detail about requests and returned results. 10. No server-delivered skills are documented; public guidance includes client workflow suggestions. 11. Whether prior agent behavior affects future outputs or tool availability is Unknown. 12. The endpoint is documented as a flat grouped tool set; no sub-server hierarchy or proxying is documented. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or universal escape-hatch tool appears in the official tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Once you've connected the Ashby MCP server, just describe what you want in plain language and your MCP client will pick the right tools and run them for you.
You do not invoke this directly, but this is what lets filtering work reliably across all supported record types.
Use this right before an interview.
This only shows your own feedback, not other interviewers'.
Drafts a note on a candidate's profile for you to confirm before saving. Can also reply to an existing note.
When you archive an application this way:
Include an archive reason when you move the application to the Archived stage.
You cannot set archive notes or archive reason custom fields.
Upcoming scheduled interviews aren’t canceled. Interview requests that haven’t been scheduled yet are closed.
Automatic activities on the Archived stage run the same way they do in the app. For example, the candidate still gets any automated archive email.
Pending feedback requests follow your organization’s setting for archived applications.
You cannot change an archive reason with the tool.
Use the submit_mcp_feedback tool in your AI client to send feedback directly to the Ashby team. Include as much detail as possible about what you asked and what the server returned.
If you do see a rate-limit error, prompt your MCP client to run fewer operations in parallel against Ashby MCP, or wait a moment before retrying.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented endpoint presents a flat set of grouped tools. No dynamic toolsets, nested servers, or proxy structure is documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list is on https://docs.ashbyhq.com/ashby-mcp-server-beta and names 17 tools; it does not state a total. actions.json contains all 17 official names, with no catalogue-only additions. The Claude connector directory lists 16 and omits submit_mcp_feedback. Other catalogues were checked as cross-checks; their differing counts or incomplete descriptions were not used to replace the official list.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim tool schemas plus initialize instructions were available to serialize; official docs supply names and summaries only.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Ashby product documentation describes broader application features such as configuring jobs, interview plans, approvals, email templates, and integrations. The documented MCP tool list does not expose those configuration operations; see the official MCP list and Ashby product documentation at https://docs.ashbyhq.com/ashby-mcp-server-beta and https://developers.ashbyhq.com/reference/introduction.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Ashby says users may set their preferred control level in the MCP client, including approval before actions; this is client-side guidance, not a documented server-enforced confirmation mechanism. It recommends reducing parallel operations or waiting after rate-limit errors. Tool input/output contracts may change without notice; the docs recommend using the public API when a stable contract is needed.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Ashby states that each user connects through separate OAuth and the server returns only data visible under that user's Ashby permissions. It says users are authenticated individually and are not represented by a shared service account. Its privacy policy describes Ashby as processing customer personal information on customer instructions.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Ashby describes the hosted connection as permission-aware and available with MCP-compatible clients. It labels the server Open Beta and says the experience may vary depending on client and model.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance and individually authenticated users are stated in official docs and OAuth metadata supports protected bearer access, but public implementation code is unavailable for independent verification. Client approval before actions is described as a client preference, with no server enforcement documented. MCP-specific logging, retention, and telemetry behavior are not stated.

contradictions: The official Ashby knowledge-base tool list names 17 tools including submit_mcp_feedback, while the Claude connector directory lists 16 and omits that feedback tool. The official list is used for actions.
observations_for_research: Official tool descriptions include at least one instruction that the AI should not directly invoke a helper (describe_object_fields), alongside user-facing workflow guidance.
The official docs tell clients that tool inputs and outputs may change without notice and direct users seeking stable contracts to the Ashby public API.
The feedback tool explicitly routes reports and suggestions to Ashby and asks the user to include what they asked and what the server returned.
notes: Inspected the prepared pages, scripts, links_check.txt, and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt first. No official public code or package was present. The official reference page and its rendered script supplied the tool names and descriptions, but not JSON schemas, annotations, initialize instructions, or tool result formats. Checked official pricing, privacy, terms, product update, Academy course, and third-party listings; unofficial or third-party catalogues were used only as cross-checks. No separate official MCP endpoint was found. Pricing page exposes a Foundations amount but does not state MCP-specific charges.
